setting: a boutique coffee roaster evaluating a subscription‑delivery platform (Crimson Roast)
prompt:
Maya Patel, our COO, will decide next week whether we move forward with the Crimson Roast subscription‑delivery platform. I need a concise brief for her that includes one clear recommendation, the three biggest ways the plan could fail, and the specific metric that would trigger us to kill the project.  

Here are the hard facts: we’re targeting 12,000 active subscribers by the end of Q4 2025, each paying $45 per month for a 12‑bag rotation. Our cost per bag is $8, and Crimson Roast charges a 12% platform fee on gross sales. We expect a monthly churn of 5% (assumption: churn will stay under 5% after the first three months). The pilot would run from Jan 15 2025 to Mar 31 2025, during which we’ll ship 3,600 bags. Our current retail sales are $600 k per quarter, and we think the subscription could add $540 k in new revenue (12,000 × $45 × 3 months ÷ 2, assuming half the target is hit in the first quarter).  

We don’t know the one‑time integration cost for linking our inventory system to Crimson’s API—vendors have quoted “in the low‑four figures,” but no exact number yet. Please give Maya a recommendation, outline the top three failure points, and state the result (e.g., churn > 7% or net profit margin < 12% over the pilot) that would make us stop or pivot.

setting: an offshore wind farm operator assessing a drone‑inspection service (Zephyr Tide)
prompt: I need a quick stress‑test of the drone‑inspection proposal before I pitch it to our CEO, Maya Patel, next week. We operate 84 turbines at the Atlantic Ridge offshore wind farm. Zephyr Tide has quoted $1,200 per sortie and estimates we’ll need 120 sorties a year, which they say totals $180,000 annually (I’m double‑checking that multiplication). The contract would run for three years starting Q3 2024, with an upfront setup fee of $45,000 for the ground control station and $12,000 per month for data‑processing software. Their marketing material claims a 90 % weather‑availability window for flights, but we know the region averages only 78 % clear‑day slots in the summer months. They also say the drones can detect blade cracks with 95 % accuracy, yet they haven’t provided any independent validation data. I’m assuming the $12,000 monthly fee covers all analytics, but I’m not sure if additional per‑image storage costs will apply. The unknown we can’t quantify yet is the regulatory approval timeline for autonomous flights in our EEZ—if it takes longer than six months, our schedule shifts. Please give me one clear recommendation for Maya, outline the main ways this plan could fail (technical, financial, regulatory), and specify the trigger that would make us abort the project (e.g., if total downtime from inspection delays exceeds five days per turbine per year).
